mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is always associated with positive 20-day forward returns on the S&P 500, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase equity valuations.
failure_condition: At least 40% of historical instances where FEDFUNDS was between 1.0% and 5.0% resulted in negative 20-day forward returns, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative 5-day forward returns on the S&P 500.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS rose by more than 0.5% over the prior 3 months, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%) predicts positive 60-day forward returns, as the market prices in a 'soft landing' scenario where monetary policy is neutralizing inflation without causing a recession.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS rose and CPIAUCSL was below 2.0%, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to increased risk aversion and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS rose for 3 consecutive months, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it signals a tight labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive 5-day forward returns on the S&P 500.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE was below 3.5%, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising industrial production (INDPRO) and falling housing starts (HOUST) predicts negative 60-day forward returns, as it signals a slowdown in manufacturing and housing demand, which reduces economic growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 0.5% in 3 months and HOUST falls > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO rose by more than 0.5% and HOUST fell by more than 0.5% over the prior 3 months, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During supply chain disruption (defined by INDPRO falling below 100 for 2 consecutive months), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to increased uncertainty and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO was below 100 for two consecutive months, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (defined by GDPC1 growth above 2.5% and INDPRO above 105), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to overvaluation and increased risk of a policy-induced slowdown.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate exceeded 2.5% in the last quarter and INDPRO was above 105, as measured by a 3-year rolling window.
